extracted.intended_audience: public relations counsel, press agents, corporate/organizational communicators, journalists, and students of public relations
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles, techniques, ethical obligations, and practical methods for counsel on public relations — i.e., how PR practitioners should plan, execute and judge campaigns to influence public opinion across institutions and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and role of the public relations counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs and supervises the activities of his clients wherever they impinge upon the daily life of the public; interprets the client to the public and the public to the client; advises on all occasions on which his client appears before the public, whether in action or as an idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The counsel's advice covers concrete actions and the use of mediums (printed, spoken, visual) — advertising, lectures, stage, pulpit, newspapers, photographs, wireless, mail, or any other form of thought communication. He must analyze problems and recommend practical measures that affect public behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established mediums of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The public can be reached only through established mediums of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and employ the most appropriate medium(s) for reaching each target public (newspapers, radio, motion pictures, lectures, direct mail, advertising, photographs, wireless/telegraph). Medium selection should match audience habits and the message's nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create concrete, verifiable signals to counter rumors
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere denial accomplishes little; overcome rumors by giving the public positive evidence of intent (e.g., renewing a key contract publicly to signal business continuity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design visible, unambiguous actions with news value to demonstrate facts — public announcements, high-profile hires, contract renewals — rather than abstract denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage prominent figures and endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use well-known persons (public officials, experts, celebrities) to amplify credibility and attract press interest (e.g., letters from Herbert Hoover, Enrico Caruso’s telegrams).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select endorsers whose reputations align with the message and whose participation produces newsworthy copy or symbolic reassurance to target publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment publics and tailor appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the public into groups (geographical, professional, business, religious, economic position, preferences) and prepare appeals directed to each relevant category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lists, direct-by-mail, different messaging and channels per segment; tailor content (ethnology for amateurs, language development for linguists, concerts for music lovers) to maximize relevance and uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make specialized material newsworthy and broadly distributable
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert treatises or technical studies into interesting stories of news value so otherwise-ignored material will be read and disseminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package technical facts into human-interest angles, abstracts, symposiums, or collated survey results; distribute to newspapers, class journals, and associations for reprinting and further distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan phased, multi-audience campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance a campaign 'little by little and phase by phase' — sequentially target different publics with adapted material until public, press and officials acquire understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map stages of persuasion across groups (mass meetings, petitions, congressional appeals, advertising, radio, motion pictures), coordinating timing and message framing to build cumulative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use events and ceremonies to generate publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage inauguration ceremonies, launches, public inaugurations (mayors exchanging first radio messages, ship launching) to create a visual and reportable event that spreads through the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design symbolic public acts that encapsulate the desired implication (friendship, unity, stability) and ensure media capture (motion and still pictures, press dispatches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalize on influential group actions to persuade others
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the cooperative action of respected groups (e.g., Fifth Avenue Association) to set an example that induces wider cooperation and lends credibility to appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure high-profile institutional participation early and publicize it widely so others emulate or accept the implied endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ surveys and expert inquiries to make opinions articulate
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission surveys or inquiries of leaders (physicians, club women, business men) to produce authoritative statements that focus attention on an issue and supply publishable material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collate responses, produce abstracts or symposiums, distribute gratis to media and organizations; use authoritative framing to shift consumption or opinion (e.g., dietary advice to increase bacon consumption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple and overlapping channels simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit all relevant avenues—newspapers, radio, lectures, motion pictures, mail, advertising, exhibitions—to reach different segments and reinforce messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate content across channels so that each reinforces others; plan for cross-media amplification and reuse of materials in suitable forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form non-partisan or broad coalitions to unify diverse groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Create committees or united appeals that gather representatives across political and social lines to present a unified, disinterested front for a cause (e.g., League of Nations committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select diverse, respected representatives; stage meetings that dramatize unity; publicize the coalition to demonstrate broad, non-partisan support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor medium and form to message and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose whether to announce changes (price policy, personnel) by telegraph, circular, advertising, book publication, or other form based on audience expectations and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess audience habits and the perceived weight of different channels — sometimes a telegraphic announcement, sometimes an extended publication — to optimize reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dramatization and symbolism to affect foreign or distant publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatize gestures (e.g., launching a ship with notable emigrant figures, transmitting messages to homeland newspapers) to influence international morale and official attitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan symbolic acts whose imagery and messages will be carried by international media and local opinion leaders back to the target country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit existing institutional credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage official letters, endorsements, or institutional backing (government departments, relief committees, professional journals) to lend authority to a message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage reputable institutions early and use their names and networks to distribute material that would otherwise lack traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public demonstrations of local desirability to sell communities or products
rubrics_metrics.description: Create community manifestations (opening post office, festivals) to prove claims about a community or product's desirability rather than merely proclaiming them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage events with national figures and publicity to transform local occurrences into nationally interesting stories that support the client's claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert latent opinion into articulated public opinion through leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and communicate with group leaders whose expressed opinions will awaken and shape dormant public sentiment (e.g., club women influencing hair fashions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find respected local or national leaders, solicit their judgments or surveys, and publicize their positions to stimulate broader adoption of an opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify publics finely for direct-by-mail and targeted appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and use lists broken down by many criteria (geography, profession, preferences, economic position) to send precisely appropriate communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit the direct-by-mail channel to reach selected individuals or sub-groups; build and maintain lists as a strategic asset for targeted campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package persuasion as education where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame advocacy as the presentation of facts and ideas of social utility to be accepted by groups — the difference between education and propaganda is largely point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize verifiable facts, expert authority and social utility to reduce the 'propaganda' label; judge the ethical merit of campaigns and avoid misleading presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical obligation to the public and negative duty to refuse harmful work
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel owes the public conscientious scrutiny; he must avoid propagating unsocial or otherwise harmful movements and refuse retainers that conflict with his standards of integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate not only client's legal case but the social consequences of public persuasion; decline work that violates public conscience or would damage social welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professional standards and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The counsel must maintain high personal and professional standards — providing conscientious, effective service to clients without placing duty to client above duty to society and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply analysis, expert training, and moral judgment akin to established professions (law, medicine); remain vigilant about the temptation to exploit strategic positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand group and herd psychology as the basis for influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion is formed by interacting forces, groups and herd behavior; counsel must understand fundamentals of public motivation and how group formations shift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use knowledge from psychology, sociology and journalism to predict malleability or stubbornness of opinions and to design appeals that work through group mechanisms rather than solely at individual level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate press tendencies and work with the press responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the nature of newspapers and reporters (news values, tendencies, dangers) in crafting messages; the press is both a conduit and a filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare copy and events that fit newsroom needs (timeliness, human interest, visual elements); avoid relying on naive denials — give press tangible news items and authoritative materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop reporter-like skills and instincts
rubrics_metrics.description: Possess qualities of a good reporter: capacity to see the picturesque or vital point of an incident and express it so others see it; analytic skill and skillful presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train in news judgment, clear writing, gathering facts, and crafting narratives; these skills are central to effective public relations counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ a wide array of practical devices (citations, exhibitions, scholarships, menus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactical measures can be diverse and mundane — citations for employers, special menus for children, exhibitions in museums, founding scholarships — chosen to influence public perception or behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select practical devices that align with client goals and that will produce visible, understandable signals to target publics; even small operational changes can have persuasive public effect.
